title: Output formats, the restricted --jq subset, --quiet, and run-without-config
expectation: `monochange discover` emits parseable JSON under `--format json`, exactly one line of JSON under `--format json-min`, and a markdown report under `--format md`; an unknown format is rejected with exit 1. The restricted `--jq` subset keeps field access and `select` working on `config --format json`, while `length` and comma-separated filters print nothing but still exit 0 (FINDINGS defect 6) — pinned so a jq upgrade that starts emitting values is caught. `--quiet` on `step validate` suppresses all output without changing execution. Bare `monochange run` errors while no `[cli.*]` commands are configured. Nothing the checks run mutates the workspace; the one scratch file is removed by the check that created it.

checks.command: monochange discover --format json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import sys, json; d = json.load(sys.stdin); assert d['packages'], d; print('discover json ok')"
checks.why: Discovery JSON is what agents and scripts parse for package ids; it must stay machine-readable end to end.

checks.command: monochange discover --format json-min > .mc-jmin.json 2>/dev/null && python3 -c "import json, pathlib; t = pathlib.Path('.mc-jmin.json').read_text(); assert len(t.splitlines()) == 1, f'expected one line, got {len(t.splitlines())}'; json.loads(t); print('json-min ok')"; rc=$?; rm -f .mc-jmin.json; exit $rc
checks.why: The minified format exists for line-oriented tooling, so its whole payload must be a single line of valid JSON.
The markdown format is the human-readable channel; pin what it actually renders (a summary heading plus list bullets) so drift is visible.
The rejected value's error must name the accepted set, because agents recover from exactly this message.
Plain field access is the documented happy path of the restricted `--jq` subset; both fixture package ids must come through.
`select` is the other supported construct; pinning it marks the boundary between what the subset does and does not evaluate.

checks.command: out=$(monochange config --format json --jq '.config.groups | length' 2>/dev/null); rc1=$?; out2=$(monochange config --format json --jq '.config.packages[].id, .config.groups[].id' 2>/dev/null); rc2=$?; test $rc1 -eq 0 && test $rc2 -eq 0 && test -z "$out" && test -z "$out2"
checks.why: The restricted subset silently prints nothing for `length` and comma-separated filters while exiting 0 — a known trap, pinned so a jq upgrade that starts emitting values for them is a loud change, not a silent one.

checks.command: quiet=$(monochange step validate --quiet 2>&1); qrc=$?; loud=$(monochange step validate 2>&1); lrc=$?; test $qrc -eq 0 && test $lrc -eq 0 && test -z "$quiet" && test -n "$loud"
checks.why: `--quiet` must suppress progress and result output completely while the command still runs and exits 0, or scripts capturing its output break.
There is nothing to run when no `[cli.*]` commands are configured, so bare `run` must fail loudly with a config error rather than exit 0 on an empty plan.
